title: Will at least one paper published in Nature, Science, or Cell list an AI system as a formally credited author before January 1, 2030?
criteria: At least one paper published in Nature, Science, or Cell formally credits an AI system as an author before 2030-01-01; this does not require AI to be primary author or to have originated and completed the research.
why: It allows any formally credited author role and includes Cell, unlike our milestone's AI-primary-authored paper in flagship Nature or Science with AI doing the research, so it is an easier event and a lower-bound signal.

title: Will an AI system be credited as the lead author of a paper in Nature or Science before 1 January 2030?
criteria: YES if, before 2030-01-01, a paper published in Nature or Science lists an AI system (not a person) as first or lead author, or the journal's editorial note describes it as primary author; otherwise NO.
why: Lead/first/primary authorship in either flagship journal by the cutoff closely matches our event, although the market does not stipulate that AI generated the research and paper end-to-end as our details require.

title: Will there be a one-person unicorn by 2030?
criteria: By end of 2030, either a public company reaches $1B market capitalization with one funder and employee, or a one-person private company raises enough to be valued above $1B, reported by a reputable source; market clarifies that contractors are allowed and only one legal employee is permitted.
why: A one-person $1B valuation does not entail $10M annual recurring revenue or less than 10 human oversight hours per week, and the market's employee/funder criteria differ from our operating-company definition.
